description: A clock divider that counts a different number of clock pulses each cycle, and a pair of pass-through switches worked by the gate it produces

params.text: Chooses whether the counter starts again as soon as it reaches its end, or counts once and stops
Sets the smallest number of clock pulses in a cycle; click and drag the display to change it
Sets how many extra clock pulses may be added to the minimum, chosen afresh each cycle; at zero every cycle is the same length

inputs.text: The pulses being counted, read high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Returns the counter to zero when the voltage rises past 2V
Passed to Output A while the gate is low
Passed to Output B while the gate is open

outputs.text: A 1ms trigger each time the counter reaches its end
High for one clock when the counter reaches its end
The opposite of the gate output: high except for the one clock at the end of the count
Carries Input A while the gate is low, and 0V otherwise, despite the maker's own note on it saying it passes while the gate is open
Carries Input B while the gate is open, and 0V otherwise, despite the maker's own note on it saying it passes while the gate is low

notes: nothing happens until a clock is patched; the module counts pulses and has no clock of its own
the counter display shows how many pulses have arrived in the current cycle
the two pass-through switches are the wrong way round in this build: Output A carries its input while the gate is low and Output B while the gate is open, the opposite of the manual
menu: Delay Gate: 1 Clock, No Delay — chooses whether the gate opens on the clock that ends the count or one clock later

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
unipolar · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
